title: Objective Orchestration Playbook — Wiring Company Goals to Cross-team Initiatives
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: As Redwood scales, company-level objectives become hard to operationalize across teams. Current gaps: inconsistent initiative scoping, lack of deterministic rollup rules, and unclear handoffs between Product / Eng / Design. Goal: deliver a lightweight, repeatable playbook and supporting artifacts that wire company objectives into a sequenced set of cross-team initiatives with measurable success criteria and explicit escalation paths. Deliverables: 1) Objective->Initiative mapping template (Confluence) with per-initiative success metrics and acceptance criteria; 2) Initiative Sequencer dashboard (Grafana prototype + CSV import) to visualize dependencies, lead time, and expected OKR contribution; 3) Quarterly sync playbook (meeting agenda, pre-read checklist, decision matrix) and an automated summary email template; 4) Ownership and escalation ladder doc; 5) Example runbook applying the playbook to runtime-1.18 release. Success criteria: - 80% of company objectives have mapped initiatives and owners by cycle planning cutover; - 90% of mapped initiatives include explicit success metrics; - Stakeholders report >70% clarity on cross-team dependencies in post-sync survey. Scope: company-level objectives and functions that touch more than one team (ENG, DX, PM, Research). Out of scope: team-internal backlog grooming, tactical sprint-level issues. Trade-offs: keep playbook minimal (1–2 pages) to encourage adoption vs building a heavy governance process. Timeline: prototype artifacts by 2026-03-01, pilot with Finance and Infra teams through 2026-03-20, iterate and publish company-wide by due_date. Links: Confluence prototype: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Objective-Orchestration-Prototype; Sequencer CSV template: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Aq_example; Related PR (dashboard prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-docs/pull/72
